description: temperature and top_p with reasoning_effort high on Claude Sonnet 4.5, an older model: with thinking on, Claude takes temperature only at 1 and top_p only from 0.95, so both are left out, as today's core leaves them out.
source: core/internal/runtime/executor/claude_executor_request.go (normalizeClaudeSamplingForUpstreamDoc: a translated request loses temperature and top_p on every model)

exceptions.reason: The new core writes a Chat stream from a Claude reply as OpenAI's API does: the model that served the reply (Claude's message.model; today's core echoes the requested name), content "" with the role in the first chunk, tool arguments as Claude streams them (today's core collects them and sends them whole), the finish reason in its own chunk, and usage only when the client asks for it with stream_options.include_usage (today's core always adds it to the last chunk and in an extra chunk).
Today's core adds metadata.user_id, a hash it derives from the request, to every request it translates to Claude; the new core does not make up a user identifier for the client.

The Claude extension sends an API key in x-api-key, as Anthropic's API defines it; today's core sends it as a bearer token whenever the base URL is not api.anthropic.com (it uses x-api-key only there).

The Claude extension sends an API key in x-api-key, as Anthropic's API defines it; today's core sends it as a bearer token whenever the base URL is not api.anthropic.com (it uses x-api-key only there).

Today's core sends no thinking for reasoning_effort on this model name; the Claude extension turns the effort into thinking by the model family's rules (a thinking budget for Claude Sonnet 4.5), as in the thinking-suffix case. With thinking on, Claude takes temperature only at 1 and top_p only from 0.95, so both cores leave out this request's temperature 0.5 and top_p 0.9.
